classes.name: Background
classes.description: Space surrounding the image and small visible gaps, such as gaps in handrails or narrow openings between wall, eave, and downpipe

classes.name: Lines
classes.description: All lines that define the image

classes.name: Roof
classes.description: Sloping and curved roofs, edges of flat roofs, exposed top slabs forming the uppermost covering of the building, and integral roof-edge components such as gutters, fascia boards, barge boards, and parapet copings

classes.name: Walls
classes.description: Primary wall surfaces of the facade, including chimneys with wall-like construction

classes.name: Glass panes
classes.description: Large glass panes and individual panes within mullioned windows, excluding glazing incorporated into doors or balustrades

classes.name: Window frames
classes.description: Window frames and mullions in single-pane and subdivided windows.

classes.name: Doors
classes.description: Ground-level doors and doors to balconies or terraces at upper levels, including their glazing

classes.name: Detailing
classes.description: Applied architectural articulation and decorative elements, including engaged columns, decorative lintels, string courses, and mouldings

classes.name: Stairs
classes.description: Stairs shown in elevation or profile

classes.name: Handrails
classes.description: Handrails associated with stairs, balconies, or terraces

classes.name: Glass balustrades
classes.description: Glass panels used as balustrades or handrail infill on stairs, balconies, decks, or terraces

classes.name: Foundation
classes.description: The foundation such as entry slabs that are visible from the front of the house

classes.name: Decks
classes.description: External occupiable slabs or platforms, including projecting, recessed, rectangular, and L-shaped decks

classes.name: Overhangs and awnings
classes.description: Projecting elements that provide shade or weather protection, including overhangs, awnings, canopies, and entrance covers, where not supported on a column

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Small ancillary, service, or technical elements, including downpipes, exterior wall lamps, chimney pots, vents, utility fixtures, and infrequently occurring elements such as mounted solar panels, as well as segments too small to categorise efficiently, including one-pixel-wide regions

interpretive_rules: Detailing vs Other: if the element contributes to the architectural articulation or ornamental composition of the facade, classify it as Detailing. If it primarily performs a small service, utility, or equipment function, classify it as Other.
Walls vs Detailing: detailing is applied to the face of the wall; walls are the primary mass surface.
Very small or functionally minor elements that cannot be consistently separated are assigned to Other.
